history.summary: A modern Shiva temple at Manjhwas village, about 20 km from Nagaur city on the Deh route. It is said to have been built by Yogi Ganeshnath in 1982, deliberately modelled on the Pashupatinath Temple of Kathmandu, Nepal. The shivalinga in the inner sanctum is of ashtadhatu (eight-metal alloy) and four aartis are performed daily. It draws large crowds on Mahashivratri and during the month of Shravan. CSV town 'Nagaur' corrected to Manjhwas village (actual site).

name: Pashupati Nath Temple
town_description: Manjhwas is a village about 20 km north of Nagaur city on the Deh route in Nagaur district, Rajasthan; its Pashupatinath-style Shiva temple is the village's main attraction and a regional pilgrimage spot.

travel.road: About 20 km from Nagaur city on the Deh route, Manjhwas village

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahashivratri and the Shravan month
visitor_information.opening_hours: Four aartis daily; no published opening hours found (verify). Media image is a Google-hosted photo associated with the Manjhwas temple but its exact provenance is unverified (flag).
